posts:
ACT public schools face chaos as class 'splitting' and severe teacher shortages spark union threats of escalating industrial action.
Evidence: Staff shortages, Class splitting, Union strikes
#Education #Australia

The government defends its 3-year 9% pay offer as a genuine attempt to lift educator salaries above inflation and secure fair conditions.
Stated Judgement: (+0.7, +0.5) — Lesser Good

Chronic underfunding and unsustainable workloads force single teachers to manage up to 90 students, causing burnout and systemic collapse.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Government pay offers mask unsustainable teacher workloads and systemic resourcing neglect.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.8, z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- AEU ACT Branch: PASS (0.8, 0.8) — Highlights real workload and staffing crises accurately.
- ACT Government: FAIL (-0.6, -0.5) — Defends inadequate offers with misleading pay claims.
ACT public school educators rejected a recent pay offer and endorsed escalating industrial action after months of unaddressed staffing shortages.

The Poison:
Spinning below-inflation real-wage packages as record salary gains ignores the immediate crisis of 90-student merged classrooms.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing HOW (bureaucratic pay metrics) with WHY (the fundamental dignity and sustainable workload of educators).

Social Physics Analysis:
Authorities manufacture administrative compliance while shifting the burden of staff shortages onto exhausted teachers through exploitative class collapsing.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between token pay offers and crushing workloads, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Administrative evasion deepens labor strife.

The Unavoidable Truth: Class splitting directly harms student learning and accelerates educator burnout.

The Unavoidable Lie: Token salary tweaks fully resolve the systemic staffing crisis.
